proof_scope: For every sufficiently large eligible prime a nonnegative sign-feasible row of normalized root at least 1+delta has mass bounded below outside every marked frequency subgroup of size less than 2n/h_p. More than half mass in that subgroup forces its positional annihilator to be monochromatic. The clique doubling argument and the exact reciprocal-count column then force the uniform gap.

For any fixed union of cosets of one frequency subgroup, the exterior of an exact sector row is either zero or has effective support at least a constant times sqrt p. The same statement holds at square order. Together with the prime mass bound this gives genuine positive exterior mass and many nonzero coordinates even for subgroups just above sqrt n.

The logarithmic translated-mask bound controls complex filtered weights with an explicit forbidden-sector leakage term. On the true larger-side endpoint, a specified Bohr arc centered opposite the mark in any sufficiently long-order direction cannot contain the bulk support up to o(p^(1/6)/log p) exceptions. This exclusion gives no unrestricted atom or signed secant bound.

Two Pick functions with sum log W give an exact L1 measure budget for signed linear tests of real mark values. The field-first inequalities on a fixed disk chain suffice for hot-to-cold marked decay without finite-field extension. The required inequalities through primes remain open.

A fixed order-12000 Chebyshev extrapolation stencil across the right half-plane is violated by more than .04 on every sufficiently large actual square. The statement is asymptotic and does not determine an explicit first square. It concerns the entire half-plane.

In degree-two algebraic comparison models the phase and hot decay coexist with genuine accessible branch points and lifted distance 2 log n plus O(1). For any prescribed rank budget all ordinary Pick tests and both Loewner tests pass at arbitrary choices of nodes within that budget. This is an actual obstruction to detection under those generic hypotheses and supplies no Paley prime counterexample.
